entries.claim: Google Play generated about 75% of Korean mobile game revenue across the App Store and Google Play in January-October 2024.

facts.context: Sensor Tower, App Store + Google Play only

entries.appliesWhen: Korea game IAP revenue in official stores only; third-party Android stores excluded.

support.excerpt: Total revenue for the first three quarters reached $3.7 billion, with Google Play generating 75% of the total. (Methodology: third-party Android market data are not included.)

counterSupport.excerpt: ONE Store press kit citing IGAWorks: ONE Store 12.6% and Apple App Store 12.3% of game transaction value over H2 2020-H1 2025; implies Apple far below 25% of a three-store total.

entries.useFor: Google Play is the primary Korean store for a game; Play listing quality matters most there.
entries.researcherNote: Contradiction in denominators: Sensor Tower's ~25% App Store share excludes ONE Store; IGAWorks (via ONE Store PR) puts Apple at 12.3% of a three-store total over a five-year window. Not directly comparable.

entries.claim: Android held 64.5% of Korea's mobile OS share in August 2026.
entries.appliesWhen: Device/web-traffic share, not spend.

support.excerpt: Statcounter Aug 2026: Android 64.49%, iOS 35.5%.
The ASO Project lists Android 73.38% (older figure, attributed on the page to Statcounter; same origin).

entries.useFor: iOS is a large minority in Korea; do not neglect App Store work.
entries.researcherNote: Android share fell from about 73% (older figure) to 64% in this data; Sensor Tower still reports Google Play at about 75% of game revenue.

entries.claim: ONE Store, per its own citation of IGAWorks data, held 12.6% of Korean game transaction value between H2 2020 and H1 2025, ahead of Apple's 12.3%.
entries.appliesWhen: Korea game transaction value across Google Play, Apple and ONE Store, five-year window.

support.excerpt: ONE Store: 12.6% game transaction share vs Apple App Store 12.3% (IGAWorks Mobile Index, 2020 H2-2025 H1); Google Play share not stated in the article.

counterSupport.excerpt: Sensor Tower's official-store data puts the App Store at roughly a quarter of Korean game revenue in 2024 (excludes ONE Store).

entries.useFor: ONE Store is a real but secondary store; only relevant if the game ships there.
entries.researcherNote: Vendor self-report; IGAWorks report itself unread; period is five years so not comparable to a single year.

entries.claim: Among the top 50 grossing games listed on both Google Play and ONE Store, ONE Store's transaction share was 49.2% in H1 2025.

facts.of: ONE Store among top-50 dual-listed games

entries.appliesWhen: Games simultaneously listed on both stores, H1 2025.

support.excerpt: 2025년 상반기 구글 플레이와 원스토어에 동시 입점된 상위 매출 50개 게임 기준으로, 원스토어의 거래액 점유율은 49.2%를 기록했다.

entries.useFor: Do not cite as ONE Store's market share.
entries.researcherNote: Selection-biased (only games on both stores) and vendor-reported; do not read as the market share.

entries.claim: RPGs generated USD 2.1 billion, 52% of Korean mobile game revenue, in January-October 2024.
entries.appliesWhen: Korea App Store + Google Play game revenue, Jan-Oct 2024.

support.excerpt: RPGs generated a staggering $2.1 billion in revenue, accounting for 52% of the total South Korean mobile game market.

entries.useFor: Korea is RPG-led; an RPG framing of a roguelike listing fits the market.

entries.claim: Legend of Mushroom, an idle RPG, earned USD 140 million in Korea, about 31% of its global revenue.

facts.of: Legend of Mushroom revenue in Korea

entries.appliesWhen: Competitor benchmark, Sensor Tower data to Oct 2024.

support.excerpt: Joy Net Games' idle RPG Legend of Mushroom generated $140 million in Korea, 31% of its global revenue (Sensor Tower).

entries.useFor: Korea is a key market for competitor Legend of Mushroom; study its Korean listing.
entries.researcherNote: The 31% figure came from the page's summary output; check exact sentence before quoting.

entries.claim: Archero 2 earned USD 14.7 million in Korea, 23% of its lifetime spend, more than any other country as of February 2025.
entries.appliesWhen: Habby competitor, soft-launched in Korea first (lifetime to early 2025).

support.excerpt: PocketGamer.biz: Korea USD 14.7M (23%), Taiwan USD 10.3M (16%), US USD 9.9M (15%); Korea got soft launch access first, of which USD 11.6M came in soft launch.

entries.useFor: A Habby roguelike earns most in Korea, so Korea listing is a prime competitor reference.
entries.researcherNote: Provider of the revenue estimate not seen; Korea's lead is partly a soft-launch head start. Japan not mentioned.

entries.claim: Sensor Tower data cited by a UA blog puts Korea, Taiwan and Japan as Capybara Go's strongest markets.
entries.appliesWhen: Habby competitor, November 2024 snapshot.

support.excerpt: The strongest countries are South Korea, Taiwan, and Japan.

entries.useFor: Capybara Go's Asian listings (KR, TW, JP) are the relevant competitor references.
entries.researcherNote: Secondary blog; underlying Sensor Tower data not seen; snapshot from launch month.

entries.claim: Since 22 March 2024 Korean law requires game publishers to show loot-box item types and probabilities in the game, on the website and in advertising and promotional materials.
entries.appliesWhen: Games offering probabilistic items in Korea, including foreign publishers.

support.excerpt: 게임물을 유통시키거나 이용에 제공할 목적으로 게임물을 제작, 배급 또는 제공하는 자는 해당 게임물과 그 인터넷 홈페이지 및 광고·선전물마다 해당 게임물 내에서 사용되는 확률형 아이템의 종류와 종류별 공급 확률정보 … 표시하여야 한다.
게임물과 인터넷 홈페이지, 광고·선전물마다 확률형 아이템 정보 등을 표시해야 합니다.
Kim & Chang: obligation effective 2024-03-22, applies to domestic and overseas providers.
Law Firm Lin: Game Industry Act Article 33(2) requires display on the game, website and advertising materials.

entries.validFor: In force 2024-03-22; Game Industry Promotion Act Art. 33(2)
entries.useFor: Any Korea-facing ad or promotional material for a game with gacha must carry the disclosure.
entries.researcherNote: Law (kr-mcst origin for statute mirror and official news), plus two independent law firms. Store-page coverage is a separate question (jk-kr-011).

entries.claim: In advertising, Korean rules require the phrase '확률형 아이템 포함' rather than the individual probabilities.
entries.appliesWhen: Game advertising and promotional materials aimed at Korea.

support.excerpt: 게임 광고·선전물에서도 '확률형 아이템 포함'이라는 문구를 표시하도록 하여 게임이용자들에게 미리 안내할 수 있도록 했다.
'확률형 아이템 포함'이라는 사실을 알리는 문구가 제시되면 됩니다.
Gamemeca: outdoor, SNS/video, online, broadcast ads and game trailers must show the phrase.

entries.useFor: Add the phrase to Korean ad creatives and trailers; agency advice is a bottom caption fixed for the whole video.
entries.researcherNote: Origins: ministry guideline as reported by three outlets (one origin) plus an ad agency's reading. Official guideline PDF text unreadable in this session.

entries.claim: Korean sources say a game's app store detail page is not an advertisement for the phrase rule, though in-store search or recommendation ads may be.
entries.appliesWhen: Store detail pages and download pages versus in-store ad placements.

support.excerpt: 앱 스토어 상세페이지는 광고 대상이 아닙니다. 다만 스토어 안에서 집행하는 검색광고와 추천 지면 광고는 광고물로 판단될 여지가 있습니다.
Gamemeca: exempt are the official homepage needed to use the game and the download page from which the game client is obtained.

entries.useFor: Do not tell the client screenshots are exempt without verification; low-risk step is still adding the phrase on paid in-store ads.
entries.researcherNote: Two origins but only an agency and a press explanation; the official MCST guideline (해설서) was not readable. Verify with the MCST guideline before advising that store screenshots need no phrase.

entries.claim: Very small ad formats, such as smartphone notification ads and app-search-result ads, are exempt from the '확률형 아이템 포함' phrase.
entries.appliesWhen: Ad formats too small to hold text, as listed in Korean guideline coverage.

support.excerpt: Gamemeca: very small banner ads such as smartphone notification ads and app-search-result ads are exempt; the standard is unclear.
Sisaweek: banners or ads where adding text is physically difficult due to size are exempt.
Wepick: notification-level small banners are given as an example where inserting the phrase is difficult.

entries.useFor: Search-result placements may be exempt, but the size threshold is unclear.
entries.researcherNote: Ministry origin plus agency reading.

entries.claim: Korea's game rating body reported 266 games in breach of loot-box disclosure among 1,255 examined by July 2024, 60% of them foreign.
entries.appliesWhen: GRAC monitoring since 22 March 2024.

support.excerpt: GRAC examined 1,255 cases since 2024-03-22, found 266 games breaking the rules, 60% foreign; 185 developers had corrected; five foreign games risk distribution bans.

entries.useFor: Enforcement is active and reaches foreign publishers.

entries.claim: Breaching the Korean loot-box disclosure duty can lead to up to two years in prison or a KRW 20 million fine after a correction order.
entries.appliesWhen: Loot-box disclosure obligations under the Game Industry Promotion Act.

support.excerpt: 시정명령 불이행 시 2년 이하의 징역 또는 2천만 원 이하의 벌금.
Kim & Chang: correction order, then up to two years' imprisonment or KRW 20 million fine.

entries.useFor: Compliance is a hard constraint for Korean creatives.

entries.claim: A 2025 amendment to the Korean Game Industry Promotion Act took effect on 1 August 2025 and applies to loot-box disclosure violations after that date.
entries.appliesWhen: Loot-box disclosure violations, Korea.

support.excerpt: 2025년 8월 1일부터 시행될 예정이며 … 시행일 이후에 발생하는 확률형 아이템 표시의무 위반행위

entries.useFor: Treat the stricter regime as current.
entries.researcherNote: Newsletter detail is in an unread attachment.

entries.claim: One Korean law firm states that the loot-box regime carries civil punitive damages of up to three times the loss.
entries.appliesWhen: Loot-box disclosure violations, Korea.

support.excerpt: Sanctions: corrective order, criminal penalty (up to 2 years or KRW 20M), civil punitive damages (within three times the damage), plus possible Fair Trade Act action.

entries.useFor: Mention as a risk only after checking the statute.
entries.researcherNote: Single law-firm newsletter; not verified against the statute text.

entries.claim: Foreign games in breach of Korean disclosure rules can be removed from Korean app markets.
entries.appliesWhen: Foreign publishers with a designated Korean domestic agent.

support.excerpt: Under the current procedure, removal from the market is possible about two months after detection.
Five foreign games risk distribution bans if makers do not comply.

entries.useFor: Compliance failure can cost the Korean listing itself.
entries.researcherNote: Two origins (law firm, GRAC via press).

entries.claim: Korean law requires each game to display the producer's name, its rating and content information.
entries.appliesWhen: Games distributed in Korea (Game Industry Promotion Act Art. 33(1)).

support.excerpt: 게임물을 유통시키거나 이용에 제공할 목적으로 게임물을 제작 또는 배급하는 자는 해당 게임물마다 … 등급 및 게임물내용정보를 표시하여야 한다.

entries.useFor: Rating display is in-game; do not add a rating mark to store screenshots without checking.
entries.researcherNote: The article ties the duty to the game itself; no source read on rating-mark placement inside store images.

entries.claim: A Korean game can get its rating from GRAC or from store self-rating (IARC), but 19+ content needs a GRAC review.
entries.appliesWhen: Rating a game for Korea.

support.excerpt: Two routes: GRAC certificate (10-15 days) or store IARC self-rating on App Store, Google Play, ONE store; 19+ content requires GRAC review regardless.

entries.useFor: Check the rating route in the store account setup; not an image matter.
entries.researcherNote: Single platform-blog source (Apps in Toss); official GRAC page not fetched.

entries.claim: Habby used the actor An Jae-hong as promotional model for Capybara Go in Korea, ahead of the 23 October 2024 launch.
entries.appliesWhen: Korean brand and UA marketing, not store images.

support.excerpt: HABBY named actor An Jae-hong (Reply 1988) promotional model; launch 2024-10-23; pre-registration on App Store and Google Play.
AppGrowing: Korea creatives invited An Jae-hong to endorse the game and explain gameplay and 'high welfare' content, unlike JP/TW/HK creatives.

entries.useFor: Korean launch marketing uses a known face; a lighter equivalent is a named voice or spokesperson, not a screenshot element.
entries.researcherNote: Origins: publisher announcement and AppGrowing's ad-library view; both about ads, not store images.

entries.claim: Capybara Go's Korean pre-registration included a prize draw for members of the official Naver lounge, with devices such as a Galaxy S24 Ultra and iPhone 16 Pro.
entries.appliesWhen: Korean pre-registration, October 2024.

support.excerpt: Pre-registration via App Store and Google Play gave various rewards; official Naver lounge members received prizes including Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, iPhone 16 Pro and Galaxy Watch 7.

entries.useFor: Korean pre-registration commonly ties into a Naver community sign-up.
entries.researcherNote: Single publisher announcement.

entries.claim: A Korean gaming-insight vendor says structured pre-registration with milestone rewards and community building measurably affects Day 1 install intent, but shows no data.
entries.appliesWhen: Korean pre-registration strategy.

support.excerpt: A structured pre-registration campaign with milestone rewards and community-building elements has a measurable impact on Day 1 install intent and first-session depth.

entries.useFor: Not evidence of effect size.
entries.researcherNote: Vendor assertion, no numbers. A claim that over 90% of top-20 Korean games ran pre-registration was not traceable and is not recorded.

entries.claim: Korean publishers run Chuseok events with login rewards, summon tickets, hanbok costumes and limited items.
entries.appliesWhen: Chuseok holiday, 2026 (24-27 Sept core).

support.excerpt: Nexon, Netmarble, NCSoft, Smilegate and others run login streaks, summon tickets, costumes and item events for Chuseok 2026.
NCSoft, Devsisters, Kakao Games, Smilegate, Pearl Abyss: login rewards of summon tickets, enhancement stones, gold; hanbok costumes; limited items; core holiday Sept 24-27, events mainly to Oct 7.

entries.useFor: A seasonal Chuseok event is normal in Korea; treat a store-image refresh as optional.
entries.researcherNote: In-game events; no effect on store-image performance measured.

entries.claim: Netmarble ran Seollal (Lunar New Year) events across 13 games in February 2026 with login bonuses, summon tickets and holiday costumes.
entries.appliesWhen: Seollal 2026, one publisher.

support.excerpt: Netmarble: Seollal events in 13 games, Feb 12-26 primary window, rewards include hero summoning tickets, SSR+ tickets, costumes.

entries.useFor: Seollal is an event window like Chuseok; free-summon rewards are the standard hook.
entries.researcherNote: Publisher self-notice, one origin.

entries.claim: A Korean ASO guide asserts that the first three screenshots determine 80% of conversion but cites no source.
entries.appliesWhen: Korean ASO commentary, 2026.

support.excerpt: 검색 결과에서 노출되는 첫 3장이 전환율의 80%를 결정합니다.

entries.useFor: Do not cite as data.
entries.researcherNote: Unsourced assertion; a Chinese blog claimed 70% (seen only as a snippet, not recorded). Do not repeat as fact.

entries.claim: The W3C Korean layout requirements (KLREQ) say Hangul is set horizontally left to right, words are separated by spaces, and line breaks may fall on character or word basis.
entries.appliesWhen: Hangul text in store image captions.

support.excerpt: Characters progress left to right, lines top to bottom; in principle words are separated by spaces; if a line ends in Hangul, breaking is done on character or word basis and the user decides.

entries.useFor: Break Korean headlines at word boundaries where possible; a native reviewer should check.
entries.researcherNote: General typography standard; no game-store study of Hangul fonts was found.
